course_position.stage_name: Consolidation, Fluency, Confidence, and Integrated Review

lesson_intent.one_sentence_goal: Recycle practical passive forms in public information and everyday instructions.
lesson_intent.real_life_context: A building notice affects laundry booking, entry codes, and shared spaces.
lesson_intent.communicative_function: Understanding a notice, explaining what is required, and deciding how to adapt.

dialogue_task.scenario: Anna and Erik read a housing notice about maintenance in the laundry room and explain what will be closed, changed, or allowed during the week.

main_focus.name: s-passive in notices and practical instructions
main_focus.description: Use and understand s-passive forms for what is done, changed, closed, or booked in a shared housing context.
main_focus.desired_presence: Use passive forms naturally 3-4 times, mostly when paraphrasing the notice.

allowed_supporting_grammar: modal verbs for obligation and permission
subordinate clauses with när and eftersom
avoid_grammar: passive alternatives with bli as a major focus

vocabulary_target.theme: housing notice and shared laundry logistics
vocabulary_target.desired_presence: Use housing and notice language as active material, with passives tied to the written information.

dialogue_shape.opening: One speaker notices new information posted in the building.
dialogue_shape.middle: They paraphrase the notice and discuss the practical consequences for their week.
dialogue_shape.ending: They agree on a new laundry plan and what to check if something is unclear.

target_complexity.repetition: passive forms should recur in natural paraphrases of the notice

focus: the main point of the housing notice
the practical consequence for laundry planning
what information still needs to be checked

sentence_focus: one sentence beginning with Enligt lappen
one sentence explaining a consequence with därför
one sentence about planning around the changed access
